title: cost-optimization-autotune-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Aisha Kaur
release_notes: Adds autotune pipeline and defaults for batching/caching, new quantization profiles for common model families, and unit-economics dashboard tooling. Backwards-compatible runtime defaults; no customer-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token unit cost for typical RLHF/chat workloads by automating sensible batching/caching defaults and surfacing unit-economics recommendations. This PR implements an autotune pipeline that suggests and applies conservative defaults for batch windows, prefix KV cache TTLs, and model quantization profiles based on historical workload telemetry. It also adds a lightweight unit-economics tool used by the Console to show expected $/1M tokens and marginal cost improvements. Scope: 1) Autotune service + controller to compute defaults from p50/p95 latency and seq-length histograms; 2) Runtime integration to accept autotune profiles and fallback rules; 3) Quantization profile registry with recommended profiles for Llama2-13B, RedLlama-7B, and open-weights variants; 4) Console dashboard endpoint and example linear widgets; 5) Tests + CI. Checklist: [x] design doc linked ENG-5421; [x] unit/integration tests; [x] canary rollout config; [x] docs stub. Non-goals: automatic forced quantization on customers without opt-in. Related: ENG-5480 for rollout policy, SUP-789 customer report that triggered this work.

canary_and_rollout: Canary: 5% traffic, 24h observation window, automatic rollback on >8% latency regression or error-rate spike. Full rollout via Console with canary-to-100% staged policy tied to rollout metric checks.
operational_notes: Default autotune pipeline runs daily; customers can opt-out per-route via route config. Autotune proposals are stored in profile registry and only applied by Dedicated/Private clusters after explicit opt-in or Console approval. Migration script included for internal profile backfill.

notes_for_release: This release enables autotune defaults and unit-economics tooling. Customers will see new 'Autotune' suggestions in the Console and can apply them per-route. No breaking changes. Recommend announcing to Early Adopters and including link to docs/optimize/autotune.md.
security_considerations: Profiles are treated as non-sensitive config and validated before application. Autotune controller requires service role with least privilege. No secrets added. Audit logs emitted for profile applies.
why_this_matters: Automating conservative batching/caching defaults and surfacing quantization recommendations is expected to reduce token spend by 10-35% for typical chat workloads while maintaining latency SLOs. The unit-econ tooling gives product teams visibility into marginal cost tradeoffs for model choices and quantization, improving decision velocity.
